subject: Post-call: perf discovery & traffic envelope (hosted vs incumbent)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Sun <alicia@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — perf discovery and traffic envelope

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations before the PoC: 

Summary of what we heard you need
- E2E (client → app → Redwood hosted API → model → app → client) targets: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 750ms for the majority of interactive endpoints.
- Streaming endpoints (incremental tokens) need to feel realtime for end-users: per-user concurrency of 1–3 streams and tail latency constraints similar to the non-streaming path.
- Typical traffic: median payload ~350 tokens; peak sustained 150 RPS; expected burst up to 500 RPS for up to 5 minutes during batch jobs.
- Critical goal: reduce p99 tail compared to current provider while keeping cost neutral or better.

What we proposed on the call
- Redwood will run a controlled 48–72 hour PoC replay using your production traces (anonymized). We'll run three scenarios: baseline mimic of current provider, streaming-heavy workload (50% streaming), and a high-concurrency soak.
- We will instrument end-to-end timing (client RTT, app service time, Redwood ingress-to-egress, model token time) and provide token-level billing and latency breakdowns.
- If p99 improvements look good we can propose a limited canary cutover with automatic fallback to your incumbent.

Open asks from us (please send before the PoC kickoff)
1) A 1–2 week sample of request traces (timestamps, latency, payload size, request ids) — even a 10k-request sample is enough to start. Prefer CSV/JSON.
2) Any rate-limiting rules or circuit-breaker behavior we should mimic.
3) Confirmation of the three endpoints you'd like us to test (will use the same auth keys you provide for read-only test mode).

Attached is a draft traffic envelope matrix I sketched during the call (20271201-traffic-envelope-draft.xlsx).

Next steps
- We'll tentatively schedule the PoC kickoff for Wednesday (Dec 8) — can you confirm availability?
- I'll publish a short PoC plan and kickoff invite once we have the traces.

Cheers,
Jonas
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20271201-traffic-envelope-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Alicia Sun <alicia@veridian.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Kim <oliver.k@veridian.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 18:35:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — perf discovery and traffic envelope

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear recap. A few data points and questions from our side: 

Traffic snapshot (last 2 weeks, anonymized)
- Median payload: 320 tokens
- Typical sustained: 120 RPS; daily peak 420 RPS (short bursts ~3–7 minutes)
- Current provider observed E2E: p95 240ms, p99 980ms (we're seeing tail spikes during 2× traffic events)

We attached a zipped sample of traces (veridian-sample-traces-2027-11.zip). The file contains request ids, client timestamps, and server-side latencies. Let us know if another format is easier.

Two questions before kickoff:
1) Streaming: do you support chunked partial responses over HTTP/2 and WebSocket-style streaming? We rely on incremental token delivery for UX and want to understand concurrency limits per session.
2) KV/prefix caching: can Redwood warm and reuse KV caches across requests for the same session in the hosted mode (we sometimes send repeated prefixes and that impacts tail latencies).

We can confirm the endpoints to test — will send those by EOD tomorrow. Dec 8 looks fine for kickoff; prefer AM Pacific.

Best,
Alicia
Head of Platform Engineering
Veridian Health

Attachment: veridian-sample-traces-2027-11.zip (trace bundle stub)

On Wed, Dec 1, 2027 at 3:02 PM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations before the PoC:...

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Internal - PoC test matrix (draft)

Internal note — copying the test matrix I sketched for the infra team so we can be ready to execute as soon as we get the traces and auth keys. Thoughts welcome: 

Test scenarios (48–72h total)
1) Baseline replay (incumbent mimic): replay sampled traces at real-time pace (scale to 1× observed RPS). Measure p50/p95/p99 and token-cost.
2) Streaming probe: convert 50% of requests to streaming; measure chunk interval, per-user concurrency tests at 1, 2, 3 streams; verify partial prefix caching and early-flush behavior.
3) Tail soak: sustained 150 RPS for 6 hours then 2× burst to 500 RPS for 10 minutes; observe failover behavior and queue depth.

Key measurement hooks
- End-to-end timers (client->ingress, ingress->egress, model tokens)
- KV cache hit rates for repeated prefixes
- Request throttling counts and 429 patterns (if any)

Runbook references: RINF-LATENCY-5 (internal) — I'll link to the checklist in Confluence once I finalize.

I'll preseed Jenkins jobs and a Grafana dashboard for Alicia to view results live.

-ben
Ben Carter
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Sun <alicia@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — perf discovery and traffic envelope

Alicia — thanks for the traces and the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and logistics: 

1) PoC scope
- 48-hour PoC starting Wed Dec 8 (09:00 PT) — baseline replay + streaming probe + tail soak.
- Deliverables: full latency breakdown (client, ingress, model, egress), p50/p95/p99 tables, per-route dashboards, and a short exec one-pager comparing cost and p99 tail against your incumbent.

2) Streaming & caching answers
- Redwood supports chunked incremental responses over HTTP/2 and a streaming WebSocket proxy layer. We'll validate per-session concurrency at 1–3 streams during the streaming probe.
- We support KV/prefix caching in hosted mode for warm caches within a session; we'll include a test to measure cache warm-up and hit rate.

3) Action items for Veridian (Alicia/Oliver)
- Share the final list of endpoints to test (by EOD tomorrow).
- Provide an API key for read-only test traffic and an anonymized 10k-request trace (we have the ZIP; if you can also send CSV it's helpful).

4) Redwood action items
- Ben will spin up the replay harness and dashboards (Ben — noted your runbook).
- I'll send a short PoC plan and a calendar invite for Dec 8 AM PT.
- We'll also include a short checklist for fallbacks (how we route to incumbent under overload).

I've attached a one-page PoC plan (redwood-poc-plan.pdf) with timeline and responsibilities. Let us know if NDA or procurement steps are needed before we begin — happy to route that separately.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (PoC plan stub)
